To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the collective dimension of privacy and data processing is an emerging layer of protection that is different from the individual and group dimensions, it represents the protection of the interests that are related to the collective dimension, it is based on a representation of the underlying interest and it is protected through a set of specific legal rules.
the right to informational privacy and the right to data protection have both an individual and a collective dimension.
the right to privacy has a collective dimension, which can be defined as a set of rights that protect the interests of groups of people from the potential risks of mass data collection.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions. How does the new dimension of data protection differ from the individual one? How does this dimension relate to the group dimension? Which are the underlying values and interests? Which are the main risks that can be addressed by this new dimension? Which are its limits and its potential?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the collective dimension of the right to informational privacy and data protection protects groups of persons against discrimination and invasion in the context of data processing and analysis.
the collective dimension of privacy and data is a set of interests that are shared by a group of persons, which is different both from the individual and from the collective interests.
the collective dimension of privacy and data privacy is a right to be protected from the harms that can derive from the use of personal information in decision-making processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the collective dimension of privacy and data privacy has to be considered as the right of a group of individuals to be treated equally in the context of a specific social situation, where they have to be considered as a whole and not as a sum of individuals.
the right to data protection has to be understood as a collective right in order to be able to address the risks of mass predictive analysis.
the collective dimension of privacy and data rights protects groups of persons and their interests from the risks of discriminatory and invasive data processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the collective dimension of privacy and data privacy is a necessary tool to ensure the effective protection of individuals and groups of people against the potential harms of mass predictive analysis.
, while the right to data protection is a personal right, it is not limited to the protection of the interests of a single data subject.

the collective dimension of privacy and data rights is an emerging layer that needs to be taken into account in order to address the challenges related to the new technologies and the new forms of analysis.
